name: webpack-resolve-fallback-node-false-for-node-protocol
hook: resolve.fallback node:false is the correct webpack 5 API for node: protocol imports
body: webpack 5's resolve.fallback with { node: false } is the correct mechanism for handling Node.js built-in module requests via the node: protocol (node:console, node:crypto, node:dns, etc.). It returns an empty object, satisfying the resolver without actually polyfilling. Do NOT use resolve.alias with a regex pattern like '^node:(.*)$' — this is treated as a literal key in webpack 5 and never matches.
why: CI failed with 'UnhandledSchemeError: Reading from node:console is not handled by plugins'. The previous approach used resolve.alias with '^node:(.*)$' which does not work because webpack 5 resolve.alias treats string keys literally, not as regex.

name: next-config-js-uses-esm-require-unavailable
hook: next.config.js is ESM — use path.resolve not require.resolve
body: next.config.js uses ESM (import at top level), so require is not available. When adding webpack resolve.alias entries that need a file path, use path.resolve(process.cwd(), ...) instead of require.resolve(...). process.cwd() gives the project root at build time.
why: CI failed with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined' at next.config.js because the file is ESM but required was used in the webpack config callback.

name: serverexternalpackages-handles-canvas
hook: @napi-rs/canvas in serverExternalPackages prevents webpack from trying to bundle it
body: Adding @napi-rs/canvas to serverExternalPackages in next.config.js is sufficient to prevent webpack from attempting to bundle the canvas native binaries. No additional webpack externals or resolve.alias for .node files is needed when serverExternalPackages is properly configured.
why: The original CI failure had .node native binary errors from canvas. Adding serverExternalPackages: ['@napi-rs/canvas'] at the Next.js config level (not webpack level) prevents webpack from even attempting to bundle those files.

name: minify-webpack-plugin-hookweberror-secondary
hook: HookWebpackError is a secondary error from minify-webpack-plugin failing to wrap an error
body: The 'HookWebpackError: _webpack.WebpackError is not a constructor' from minify-webpack-plugin is a SECONDARY error that occurs when the minifier tries to wrap an underlying webpack error but can't construct the error object. This can happen when complex webpack configurations (like regex externals for .node files) produce an error state that the minifier can't properly serialize. The fix is to simplify the webpack config to only what's essential — the root cause is the complex config, not the error wrapper.
why: CI was failing with HookWebpackError after adding .node alias and canvas regex externals. Simplifying to just undici external + node:false fallback fixed it, proving the issue was the complex config interacting with minify-webpack-plugin, not the individual settings.

name: nextjs15-isServer-isNodeOrEdgeCompilation
hook: Next.js 15 webpack config: isServer is isNodeOrEdgeCompilation — use !isClient for non-server-only configs
body: In Next.js 15.5.9, the isServer parameter passed to the webpack config function is actually set to isNodeOrEdgeCompilation (isNodeServer || isEdgeServer), meaning isServer=true for BOTH Node server builds AND Edge builds. So 'if (!isServer)' is false for Edge builds, causing the webpack config to be skipped for Edge. Use 'if (!isClient)' instead to correctly identify browser-only builds, allowing the config to also apply to Edge builds. isClient=true only for browser builds; false for both server and Edge.
why: CI was still failing with node:console and .node native binary errors even though the webpack config had 'if (!isServer)' with resolve.fallback.node:false. The condition was false for Edge builds (isServer=true for Edge) so the config was skipped, causing the errors.
